title: Waste Management: A Modern and Sustainable Approach
overview: In the 21st century, sustainable waste management goes beyond just safe disposal; it also focuses on resource management and recovery. This course is designed for individuals involved in waste production or handling, helping them adopt sustainable and cost-effective waste management practices, both locally and nationally. The course follows the principles of the waste management hierarchy, emphasizing the idea of waste as a resource, which not only helps protect the environment but also maximizes profit. Participants will explore strategies for waste prevention, re-use, and recycling, as well as identify opportunities for energy generation from biological waste, such as food waste.
audience: This course is ideal for waste managers and supervisors, including those in industries that produce waste (e.g., manufacturing, retail). It is also suitable for municipal waste managers, waste planners (both private and public sector), and anyone interested in exploring modern approaches to waste management.
methodology: This highly interactive course includes group discussions, case studies, and syndicate work. It also provides practical exercises to enable participants to apply their newly acquired knowledge and skills in real-world waste management scenarios.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Understand and apply the waste management hierarchy in the context of sustainable waste management and the circular economy.
Implement sustainable waste management principles, specifically in a Middle Eastern context.
Explore re-use and recycling possibilities to manage waste-related environmental risks through a risk-based approach.
Investigate waste recovery methods, including anaerobic digestion and energy generation from waste incineration.
Assess the environmental impacts of landfill waste disposal and explore sustainable alternatives.
